subject: Urgent: Vectra production surge — 5xx/429 spike after model patch
messages:
From: Alice Green <alice.green@vectra.ai>
To: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>; Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: vectra-ops@vectra.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent 5xx/429 spike on /v1/generate after rollout

Hi KarThik / Grace,

We started seeing a sudden spike in 5xx and 429 responses to our production traffic around 07:40 PT. Traffic pattern looks normal on our side (no surge), but our users see timeouts and many clients are retrying aggressively. Error rate peaked at ~18% and p95 latency jumped from 220ms to ~3.2s.

You rolled model v3.2-quant-q4_1 for our pool earlier this morning per the canary plan. Can you confirm whether that rollout included the new CUDA kernel change (cuda-kern-v2) referenced in the release notes? We have a business-critical contract and this is already impacting live traffic.

We're opening an incident on our side (PD-4821) and are prepared to divert traffic if you recommend rollback.

Attached: grafana screenshot, sample hot request traces.

Thanks,
Alice
Director, Platform Engineering
Vectra AI
From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Green <alice.green@vectra.ai>; Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx/429 spike on /v1/generate after rollout

Alice — thank you for flagging this. I’m standing up a coordinated response now. Quick summary of what I’ve pulled:
- Our deployment pipeline pushed model v3.2 + quant profile q4_1 to the vectra-prod pool at 06:52 PT; kernel selector then favorably chose cuda-kern-v2 for longer contexts.
- Monitoring shows a rapid rise in 5xx and 429s starting ~07:38 and a spike in request retries between 07:40–07:55.

Immediate plan:
1) Marissa / SRE to check serving hosts for signs of retry amplification and OOMs.
2) Jonas / Runtime to validate kernel fallbacks and KV-cache interactions — possibility that q4_1 interacts badly with the new kernel.
3) If we can't identify a quick mitigation in 30 min, we will roll back the v3.2 deployment to v3.1 for the Vectra pool.

Grace — I’ll need you to prep a short customer note for Vectra execs; they asked to loop in procurement if this looks like an SLA breach.

I’m on PD-bridge and will update.

— KarThik
Senior Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>; Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx/429 spike on /v1/generate after rollout

On PD bridge now (PD-4821). Initial SRE notes: hosts serving the vectra-prod pool show transient connection errors to a subset of GPUs and heavy enqueue latencies in the runtime queue. No OOMs observed, but there are repeated retransmits from the client side (retry loop).

I pulled hotlogs-20270809.txt (attached) with a stack of server-side traces showing repeated request entry -> enqueue -> timeout -> client retry. The retry storm is amplifying our tail latency. Two quick mitigations I can test now (will execute with Jonas):
- Option A: Soft throttle client burst window for the Vectra pool (rate-limit 10% of bursts) — reduces retry amplification quickly but adds some client-side throttling.
- Option B: Immediate rollback to v3.1 for the Vectra pool (fast, likely to restore prior behavior).

Given the business impact and the unclear interaction between q4_1 and cuda-kern-v2, I recommend Option B unless Jonas finds a narrow mitigation.

Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx/429 spike on /v1/generate after rollout

Quick findings from runtime triage:
- Reproduced a high tail latency case in a staging-like environment when running v3.2 + q4_1 with cuda-kern-v2 for sequences >1024 tokens. The kernel path appears to allocate a temporary workspace that increases enqueue time under load; with aggressive client retries the queue degrades and yields 429s.
- The quant-profile diff includes a small change in KV cache layout (see quant-profile-diff.patch attached) that increases per-request CPU post-processing in our current code path. Combined, the kernel workspace + extra CPU work creates a window where worker threads stall and return 5xx/429.

Action taken:
- I’ve paused any further rollout for the global rollout job and scheduled an immediate controlled rollback for the Vectra pool.
- If rollback to v3.1 is started now, estimate 10–12 minutes to fully drain and revert.

I’ll continue instrumenting possible microfixes but we should rollback and then run a gated lab repro with controlled kernel config.

Jonas
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Green <alice.green@vectra.ai>
Cc: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx/429 spike on /v1/generate after rollout

Alice — thank you for the quick alert and patience as we investigate. We are initiating a rollback of v3.2 -> v3.1 for your reserved pool now; estimated completion ~09:30 PT.

We will:
- Send a post-incident summary within 48 hours with root cause analysis and a staged remediation plan (either a kernel config pin or an updated q4 profile that avoids the workspace allocation path).
- Offer a one-time credit for the impacted hour(s) given the SLA risk — I’ll coordinate with finance and procurement and send a formal note.

If you prefer, we can also divert traffic to an isolated fallback pool while we fully validate the fix; let us know if you want that.

Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Green <alice.green@vectra.ai>; Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx/429 spike on /v1/generate after rollout — Recovery and next steps

Update: rollback to v3.1 completed at 09:28 PT for the Vectra pool. Error rates returned to baseline within 4 minutes of the revert; p95 latency returned to ~240ms. Marissa validated that the retry storm reduced and no further 5xx/429 events are observed in the 3-hour window post-rollback.

Next steps / deliverables:
- Jonas to run a reproduction matrix in lab with v3.2 + q4_1 under different kernel selectors (cuda-kern-v1/v2) and token lengths; deliver artifacts and RCA in 48 hours.
- Marissa to propose a safe rollout gating checklist that includes: (1) kernel workspace smoke test, (2) KV-cache post-processing timebound, (3) immediate per-pool rollback button and automated traffic diversion.
- Grace to share the credit/contract remediation language with Vectra procurement and close the communication loop.

I’ll attach the incident artifacts to the HubSpot ticket and mark this as a Sev2 internal incident for follow-up.

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination.

— KarThik
Senior Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
